summary: Ripasudil is a Rho-associated coiled-coil kinase (ROCK) inhibitor formulated as 0.4% eye drops to lower intraocular pressure in glaucoma and ocular hypertension. By inhibiting ROCK it relaxes the trabecular meshwork and increases conventional (trabecular) aqueous-humor outflow, a mechanism distinct from prostaglandin analogues and beta-blockers. It is approved in Japan (and some Asian markets) as Glanatec and is typically added when existing therapy is insufficient. Conjunctival hyperemia (redness) is the most common, usually transient, adverse effect. Ripasudil is NOT FDA-approved; this record is based on the Japanese prescribing information and literature rather than an FDA label.
indications: Glaucoma and ocular hypertension when other therapeutic agents are insufficiently effective or cannot be used (per Japanese approval)

dosage.d: 1 drop of 0.4% ripasudil solution into the conjunctival sac of the affected eye(s) twice daily
dosage.n: Typically morning and evening; usually added to existing IOP-lowering therapy

dosage.d: Space different eye drops by at least 5 minutes
dosage.n: Administer ripasudil last or per ophthalmologist instruction

admin: Wash hands; instill one drop into the lower conjunctival sac without touching the eye with the dropper tip
Apply gentle pressure to the inner corner (punctal occlusion) for about a minute to limit systemic absorption
Wait at least 5 minutes between different eye drops
Remove contact lenses before instillation and reinsert after about 15 minutes if appropriate
Do not use if the solution is discolored or the seal is broken
moa: Ripasudil inhibits Rho-associated coiled-coil-containing protein kinase (ROCK), an enzyme that regulates actomyosin contraction and cytoskeletal tension in trabecular meshwork and Schlemm's canal cells. ROCK inhibition relaxes these cells and reduces resistance in the conventional outflow pathway, increasing trabecular aqueous-humor outflow and thereby lowering intraocular pressure.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to ripasudil or any excipient
relative: Active ocular infection or inflammation (treat first)
Contact lens wear during instillation (preservative considerations)
monitor: Signs of allergic/contact dermatitis of the eyelids

preg: Safety in pregnancy is not established and human data are limited. Systemic absorption from ophthalmic dosing is low. Use during pregnancy only if the expected benefit justifies the potential risk.
lact: It is not known whether ripasudil is excreted in human milk; systemic exposure from eye drops is minimal. Use with caution during breastfeeding and consider punctal occlusion to limit absorption.
renal: No specific dose adjustment is required because systemic absorption from topical ocular dosing is minimal.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment is required because systemic absorption from topical ocular dosing is minimal.

major: No major systemic drug interactions established (minimal systemic absorption)
moderate: Other topical ocular medications - separate instillation by at least 5 minutes to avoid washout
minor: Additive IOP-lowering when combined with prostaglandin analogues, beta-blockers or carbonic anhydrase inhibitors (intended adjunctive effect)
interactions.alcohol: No relevant interaction with topical ophthalmic use
interactions.diagnostics: Transient conjunctival hyperemia may complicate slit-lamp assessment shortly after instillation

serious: Allergic blepharitis / contact dermatitis of the eyelids
emergency: Severe allergic reaction with marked eyelid swelling (rare)

monitoring: Conjunctival hyperemia and any allergic blepharitis/dermatitis
counsel: Put one drop in the affected eye(s) twice a day, usually morning and evening
Expect temporary eye redness shortly after using the drops - it usually settles within a couple of hours
Press gently on the inner corner of the eye for a minute after instilling to keep the medicine in the eye
Wait at least 5 minutes between different eye drops, and remove contact lenses before use
Report eyelid swelling, persistent irritation, or worsening redness, and do not let the dropper tip touch your eye
pk: IOP reduction within about 1-2 hours of instillation
Peak IOP-lowering effect approximately 2 hours after dosing
Rapidly metabolised ocularly; systemic plasma levels very low with short half-life
Store at room temperature, protect from light; keep the bottle tightly closed and discard after the in-use period per the label
pearls: Ripasudil is NOT FDA-approved - it is approved in Japan as Glanatec; this record is based on the Japanese prescribing information and literature, not an FDA label
It is the first clinically approved ROCK inhibitor for glaucoma and works by increasing conventional (trabecular) outflow - a mechanism complementary to prostaglandin analogues and beta-blockers
Transient conjunctival hyperemia is very common and expected; it usually resolves within a couple of hours and is not a reason to stop unless severe/persistent
Used mainly as add-on therapy when other agents are insufficient
Use punctal occlusion and 5-minute spacing between drops to optimise effect and minimise washout
missed: If you miss a dose, instill it as soon as you remember. If it is nearly time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your usual twice-daily schedule. Do not put in extra drops to make up for a missed dose.
overdose: Topical overdose (extra drops) is unlikely to cause systemic harm given minimal absorption; it may increase transient ocular redness and irritation. Flush the eye with lukewarm water if excessive drops were instilled, and provide supportive ocular care. There is no specific antidote.
